title: De Morgan: not-(p or q) implies not-p and not-q
statement: If not-(p or q) holds, then not-p and not-q both hold.

formal.statement: theorem demorgan_not_or : ((x0 : Prop) -> ((x1 : Prop) -> ((x2 : ((x2 : Or x0 x1) -> False)) -> And (((x3 : x0) -> False)) (((x3 : x1) -> False)))))

evidence.supports: If not-(p or q) holds, then not-p and not-q both hold.
evidence.checker_command: test "$(cargo run -q -p axeyum-lean-kernel --example nat_theorem_inventory -- demorgan_not_or 2>/dev/null | grep -Ec '^demorgan_not_or[[:space:]]')" -ge 1
evidence.notes: `build_logic_prelude` (built first by `build_nat_prelude`, which `nat_theorem_inventory` constructs) admits `demorgan_not_or` only through the trusted kernel gate, so this line in the tool's output IS the type-check. Anchored with `grep -Ec '^demorgan_not_or[[:space:]]'` on the tool's own substring-filtered output, matching exactly one row; a name that does not exist makes both the tool's argument filter and the anchored grep fail (verified both ways 2026-08-25).

evidence.supports: axiom_footprint: [] -- the logic environment admits no trusted declaration
evidence.notes: Reports `logic: axiom=0 opaque=0 quotient=0 total_trusted=0`, over the full trusted surface (`Axiom` + `Opaque` + `Quotient`), not `Declaration::Axiom` alone. The enumeration is per-environment, so it bounds this theorem's footprint: a proof admitted into an environment cannot depend on a trusted declaration the environment does not contain. `logic` is the isolated, intuitionistic core (`build_logic_prelude` alone) that `nat` nests -- measured 2026-08-25 with `nat_axiom_inventory --require-axiom-free logic`.

provenance.source: read off the kernel by `nat_theorem_inventory`, not transcribed; statement authored here

prior_art.citation: Standard intuitionistic/classical propositional logic (natural deduction); no single primary source.
prior_art.establishes: One of De Morgan's laws; intuitionistically valid in this direction.
prior_art.attribution: standard textbook material; this lane did not consult a primary source

notes: Part of the `logic` prelude's first fact registrations (2026-08-25): the classical/`Decidable`/`Or`/`Iff`/`Bool`/`And` package had zero kernel-lean facts despite being the foundation every other prelude nests. `logic` is intuitionistic and axiom-free (measured: axiom=0 opaque=0 quotient=0), so this is a genuinely axiom-free kernel proof, distinct from and stronger than an `smt-term-level` truth-table check of the same-shaped statement (see e.g. F:peirce-law), which cannot certify axiom-freedom at all. Registered together with the `nat_axiom_inventory` coverage fix that extended it to build `cpoint`, the crate's ninth prelude.
